nonLabourLines.description: Legacy Oracle migration tooling & one-off ETL infra
Contingency for FX data feed subscription (multi-currency)

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available yet for this project; estimate is based on backlog scope and rate card only.

Unestimated backlog items were sized by analogy to similarly-described estimated items (e.g. PW-2 Design system ~ sized like an 8-point UI item; PW-8 Legacy migration sized as a large multi-week effort due to volume of records; PW-4, PW-6, PW-10, PW-14, PW-16, PW-18, PW-20, PW-22, PW-24 similarly analogised to 5-8 point equivalents).

Backend Developer capacity is 1.5 FTE (~240 hrs/month); 780 hours implies roughly 3.25 months of full backend capacity dedicated mostly to this backlog, which is tight given the number of backend-heavy items (auth, RBAC, payments, migration, audit, search, rate limiting) — flagged as a thinly-staffed role relative to backlog size.

DevOps Engineer is only 0.4 FTE (~64 hrs/month); 160 hours (~2.5 months of that capacity) covers CI/staging setup, migration infra support and observability but leaves little slack for unplanned infra work — flagged as thin staffing.
QA Engineer at 0.6 FTE is assumed to test incrementally alongside development rather than in a single hardening phase; 310 hours (~3.2 months at that FTE) is allocated across the whole backlog.
Frontend Developer is 1.0 FTE; 620 hours (~3.9 months) covers the component library, dashboard, invoice views, accessibility pass, responsive layout and search UI.

PW-7 (Payment provider integration) and PW-8 (Legacy data migration) are treated as the highest-risk, highest-effort items given external dependencies (Stripe, Oracle legacy schema) and are the main drivers of the Pessimistic scenario spread.

Non-labour costs are one-off/setup costs (migration tooling, Stripe sandbox/PCI review, staging infra for first 3 months, accessibility audit, FX feed) rather than recurring run costs beyond the estimate window.
Priority breakdown allocates labour + non-labour cost proportionally to the effort assumed for tasks in each priority band, using points where given and analogy sizing where not.
Low-priority items (PW-12, PW-18, PW-19, PW-23, PW-24) are assumed deferrable and are costed at minimal allocated hours, making them the first candidates for descoping if budget is constrained.
input.reasoning: Sized the 24 backlog items by combining given story points with analogy-based sizing for the 10 unestimated items, then translated total relative effort into hours per role based on task nature (backend-heavy: auth, RBAC, payments, migration, audit, search, rate limiting, observability; frontend-heavy: dashboard, invoice views, design system, accessibility, responsive layout; QA spread across all features incrementally; DevOps concentrated on CI/staging setup, migration infra and observability). Checked resulting hours against each role's FTE availability over an assumed ~4-month delivery window and flagged Backend and DevOps as thinly staffed relative to backlog scope. Added one-off non-labour costs for the riskiest external-dependency items (Stripe/PCI, Oracle migration tooling, accessibility audit, FX feed, staging infra). Built three scenarios: Most Likely equals the sum of labour + non-labour line items; Optimistic assumes ~18% efficiency gains (less rework, migration goes smoothly, fewer QA cycles); Pessimistic assumes ~22% overrun (migration and payment integration risks materialize, additional QA/hardening cycles needed). Priority breakdown apportions the Most Likely total across Urgent/High/Medium/Low bands based on relative backlog effort. Recommended reductions target descoping/deferring low-priority items and trimming non-critical scope to control cost without touching Urgent/High items.

reductions.description: Defer PW-18 (Admin back-office), PW-19 (Usage analytics), PW-24 (Decommission legacy portal) to a later phase — all Low priority and not required for initial go-live.
reductions.effect: Removes roughly 90-100 backend/frontend/QA hours from the current scope; legacy portal can keep running in parallel a bit longer.

reductions.description: Descope PW-23 (Contract tests against helpdesk API) from this phase; rely on manual regression checks against helpdesk integration until contract testing is justified by incident history.
reductions.effect: Removes an isolated QA/backend effort item with no direct end-user impact in the short term.

reductions.description: Reduce PW-14 (Multi-currency support) to USD+EUR only for launch, deferring PLN and daily FX automation to a follow-up release.
reductions.effect: Cuts backend and QA effort on FX rate handling and settlement logic by roughly a third; removes FX data feed contingency cost.

reductions.description: Run PW-8 (Legacy data migration) as a phased migration (recent 12 months of invoices first, historical data in a second pass after go-live) instead of a single big-bang migration.
reductions.effect: Lowers initial ETL tooling and backend/DevOps effort by reducing the volume and validation complexity handled before launch; remaining historical data migrated post-launch.

reductions.description: Use an off-the-shelf Angular component library (e.g. Angular Material) instead of building a fully custom design system in PW-2.
reductions.effect: Cuts frontend hours spent on building/theming custom components; some customization effort still required but core components are pre-built.
